newsitem.title: USA: U.S. producer lobbyist goes to Oklahoma commission.
newsitem.headline: U.S. producer lobbyist goes to Oklahoma commission.

text.p: Independent Petroleum Association of America said Tuesday its president Denise Bode was leaving to take a seat on the Oklahoma Corporation Commission.
The commission regulates the state's oil, gas, public utilities, and transportation industries.
An IPAA spokesman said no one was under consideration yet to replace Bode, who planned to leave after August 1.

Under Bode's leadership since 1991, independent oil and gas producers have pressed lawmakers for oil import fees, royalty and tax breaks, and changes in oil spill prevention laws to help keep small producers in business.

"Immediately upon her arrival, Denise took Washington by storm changing the image of America's independent oil and gas producers and giving Cnogress and the administration new reasons to preserve and stimulate domestic oil and gas production," IPAA chairman Lew Ward said in a statement.
Ward and IPAA vice chairman were not immediately available to comment on who might replace Bode.
